profile.summary: AlphaPeptDeep (package name peptdeep) is a Python framework for predicting properties of peptides from their sequence. Its built-in pretrained models take a peptide sequence, its modifications, precursor charge, collision energy and instrument type, and predict the MS2 fragment intensities, the retention time and the collision cross section. The usual output is a predicted spectral library, for example built from a FASTA file, for use in peptide identification.

summary_quotes.text:
It contains some built-in models such as retention time (RT), collision
cross section (CCS), and tandem mass spectrum (MS2) prediction for given
peptides. With these models, one can easily generate a predicted library
from fasta files.
Here we introduce AlphaPeptDeep, a modular Python framework built on the PyTorch DL library that learns and predicts the properties of peptides
AlphaPeptDeep contains pre-trained models for predicting MS2 intensities, retention time (RT), and collisional cross sections (CCS) of arbitrary peptide sequences or entire proteomes.
Meta embedding refers to the embedding of meta information such as precursor charge states, collisional energies, instrument types, and other non-sequential inputs.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The MS2 model is built on four transformer layers with a hidden size of 256. For each peptide of length n it outputs intensities for (n-1) cleavage positions and eight fragment types: singly and doubly charged b and y ions and their modification-associated neutral losses. The retention time and collision cross section models are smaller: a CNN layer followed by two bidirectional LSTM layers. Modifications are represented by their chemical composition, so a modification the model has not seen can still be encoded. Training intensities are normalised by the highest matched intensity in each spectrum, so predictions lie between zero and one. The authors stress transfer learning: refining a pretrained model takes minutes and is possible without a GPU.
sections.source_locator: paper: Fig. 2 caption, MS2 model, Methods

quotes.text: The MS2 model is built on four transformer layers, and the RT/CCS models consist of a convolutional neural network (CNN) layer followed by two bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) layers.
The hidden layer size of transformers is 256. The total number of the model parameters is 3,988,974.
and 8 refers to eight fragment types
All matched b/y fragment intensities in the training and testing datasets were normalized by dividing by the highest matched intensity for each spectrum.
AlphaPeptDeep represents post-translational modifications in a generic manner, even if only the chemical composition is known.
Transfer learning from a pre-trained model is feasible within minutes, even without GPU.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The pretrained models are not versioned as separate checkpoints on the page: peptdeep downloads a single pretrained_models.zip from the repository's pre-trained-models release when it is first used, and the settings file names its URL in model_url. The MS2 model has several variants selected by model_type, which can be generic, phos, hla or digly, and separate releases exist for other labels, for example dimethyl-labelled peptides. External model files can be given instead with external_ms2_model, external_rt_model and external_ccs_model. A result should name the peptdeep version and the model type; this page read the repository at commit 8e9eba6e.

sections.title: How the benchmark used it
sections.body: PepSpecBench describes AlphaPeptDeep as a modular Transformer of about 1.8M parameters and retrained it, with the other five baselines, on the benchmark data under backbone-disjoint splits. That figure and those results therefore describe the benchmark's own retrained model, not the pretrained model shipped with peptdeep, whose MS2 model the paper states has 3,988,974 parameters.

quotes.text: (modular Transformer,

All baselines are retrained on the benchmark data under the Backbone-Disjoint splits described above.

run_guide.summary: Install peptdeep, let it download the pretrained models, and predict a spectral library from a settings file.
prerequisites: Python, with Python 3.8 or 3.9 recommended in the README for the pip install.
A GPU is optional: the README gives a separate command to install the GPU build of PyTorch, and the default settings file sets torch_device to gpu.
Internet access for the pretrained_models.zip download on first use.
An input file for the library, for example a FASTA file named in the library section of the settings file.

steps.title: Install peptdeep
steps.explanation: Installs the package into an existing Python environment, as the README's pip installation section gives it.

quotes.text: pip install peptdeep

steps.title: Install the pretrained models
steps.explanation: Downloads and installs the pretrained MS2, RT and CCS models from the repository's pre-trained-models release. The README says this also happens automatically the first time peptdeep is used.

quotes.text: peptdeep install-models [--model-file url_or_local_model_zip] --overwrite True

When run for the first time, peptdeep will download and install models
defined in ‘model_url’ in the default yaml settings

steps.title: Export a settings file
steps.explanation: Writes the default settings as a template. The README says to edit this file before running other commands: the library section names the input files, and the model_mgr section sets the collision energy, instrument and model type.

quotes.text: peptdeep export-settings /path/to/settings.yaml

This command will export the default settings into the `settings.yaml`
as a template, users can edit the yaml file to run other commands.

default_nce: 30.0
  default_instrument: Lumos

steps.title: Predict a spectral library
steps.explanation: Predicts a spectral library for the inputs named in the library section of the settings file. The README's command form is 'peptdeep library settings_yaml'.

quotes.text: peptdeep library settings_yaml

This command will predict a spectral library for given settings_yaml
file

outputs: A predicted spectral library for the peptides derived from the input files, with MS2 fragment intensities, retention times and collision cross sections. The output location is set in the library section of the settings file.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The settings file must be edited between steps three and four to name the input files; the README does not give a complete worked settings file.
The README says the first run of a fresh installation is slow because some functions still need compilation.
